mechanism_narrative: Sustained decline in WORKPLACES mobility (-29.4% at t-0w) signals continued remote work adoption. This reduces weekday commuting anchors and associated retail-recreation visits, driving RETAIL_REC further negative over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES declined from -24.0% to -29.4% over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days exceeds RETAIL_REC mean over last 28 days, or WORKPLACES reverses to above -20% within two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Rising RESIDENTIAL mobility (+14.3% at t-0w, up from +9.7%) indicates households consolidating at home. This behavioral shift reduces discretionary retail-recreation trips as people substitute home-based activities, suppressing RETAIL_REC recovery.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL exceeds +12% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from +9.7% to +14.3% over four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL declines below +10% within one week and RETAIL_REC rises above -35% within two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility collapse (-50.0% at t-0w, worsening from -40.6%) eliminates the primary access channel to retail-recreation destinations. Reduced transit accessibility directly constrains RETAIL_REC recovery regardless of demand, producing sustained negative mobility.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -45% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT declined from -40.6% to -50.0% over four weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT recovers above -35% within one week, or RETAIL_REC rises above -30% despite TRANSIT remaining below -45%.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent collapse in both TRANSIT (-50.0%) and WORKPLACES (-29.4%) signals coordinated mobility restrictions (lockdown tightening). The interaction of reduced commuting infrastructure and workplace closures creates a dual suppression effect on retail-recreation access and demand, preventing RETAIL_REC recovery.
evidence_refs: fact:Both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES declined sharply in t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: Either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES recovers above threshold within one week, or RETAIL_REC rises above -35% while both remain below thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility volatility (from +29.7% at t-2w to -2.6% at t-0w) indicates outdoor-activity substitution is collapsing. As weather improves and restrictions tighten, households shift from parks to home-based activities, reducing overall mobility appetite including retail-recreation.
candidate_trigger: PARKS declines more than 20 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from +29.7% to -2.3% to -2.6% over three weeks
failure_condition: PARKS rebounds above +10% within one week and RETAIL_REC simultaneously rises above -40%.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM stability (around -7% to -8%) combined with RETAIL_REC collapse (-46.1%) indicates essential-goods shopping is protected while discretionary retail is suppressed. This divergence reflects policy prioritization of essential mobility, constraining RETAIL_REC recovery to essential-only levels.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains within -5% to -10% while RETAIL_REC < -40%
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stable at -7% to -8% while RETAIL_REC declined to -46.1%
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM declines below -15% or RETAIL_REC rises above -35% while GROCERY_PHARM remains stable.

mechanism_narrative: March seasonal patterns in Lombardy show RETAIL_REC at -46.1% despite mild weather improving. This suggests policy restrictions override seasonal reopening signals. Without policy reversal, seasonal recovery cannot overcome restriction-driven suppression, keeping RETAIL_REC negative.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC at -46.1% in mid-March despite typical spring recovery season
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -30% within two weeks, or PARKS rebounds above +15% while RETAIL_REC remains below -40%.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction of elevated RESIDENTIAL mobility (+14.3%) and collapsed TRANSIT (-50.0%) creates a regime where households are both incentivized to stay home and unable to easily access retail destinations. This dual constraint produces a strong suppression effect on RETAIL_REC that persists until either TRANSIT recovers or RESIDENTIAL normalizes.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL > +12% AND TRANSIT < -45% simultaneously for one week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at +14.3% and TRANSIT at -50.0% in t-0w
failure_condition: TRANSIT recovers above -40% within one week, or RESIDENTIAL falls below +10% within one week, or RETAIL_REC rises above -35% despite both conditions holding.
